Nothing at Petra's Treasury was built. It was carved, top-down, out of one cliff. 🏜️ Watch it in 25 seconds. ⏱️

The Nabataeans cut a platform at the very top of the rock, then chiselled their way down with simple iron chisels and hammers, freeing columns, a round tholos and an urn from solid stone. Small hand-size holes up both sides may have worked like a stone ladder. No mistakes allowed: you can't add rock back.

The twist: those pockmarks on the urn are bullet holes. Locals shot at it believing a king's treasure was hidden inside. That's why it's called "the Treasury".

Would you have shot it too? Yes or no 👇

yt_title: How Petra's Treasury Was Carved: Top-Down From One Cliff #shorts
yt_description:
Al-Khazneh ("the Treasury") at Petra was carved during the reign of Nabataean king Aretas IV (9 BC–AD 40), top-down from a rock-cut platform at the top of the cliff, with simple iron chisels and hammers. Hand-size holes up the sides may have served like scaffolding. The small holes on the central urn are bullet holes: Bedouins believed it held a king's treasure. Its original purpose is uncertain (temple / royal tomb).
